details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1447-1791 (also .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:227-235, 234, 819-821) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Base-keyed dedup (1727-1739) and the open-issue cap (1789) read an OPEN_TRIAGE snapshot fetched once at 1447. The post step then runs `gh issue create` (check_failure_triage.yml:819-821) without listing open issues again, while the concurrency group is per PR and check (check_failure_triage.yml:234). As a result, concurrent runs for different PRs failing the same check against the same base all miss each other's issue.
  WHY: Several PRs each file an issue with the identical `sha256("<repo>|base=<ref>|check=<check>")` fingerprint and can push the open count past CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_MAX_OPEN_ISSUES together. This defeats Goal 1 ("one breakage files one issue") and the changelog claim "17 before, 1 now". All reviewers that gave a severity rated it MAJOR; google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite also listed it under SECURITY with no severity.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1471-1490,1729-1734 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A supersede candidate recorded at 1478-1484 (SUPERSEDE_OLD_ISSUE set, EXISTING cleared) is silently dropped when the run then exits 0 with `skip reason=base_triage_tracked` at 1729-1734. No metadata is written, so the supersede close never runs.
  WHY: The stale ai:blocked per-PR issue stays open indefinitely and counts toward the CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_MAX_OPEN_ISSUES cap at line 1789. That fills the default cap of 5 sooner and suppresses unrelated filings, and it drops the #8671 supersede contract for this path.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:1120,1132-1136 (owner from scripts/unblock_actions.py:253-271 ci_owner_candidate; scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1637-1643) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: A base-keyed triage issue keeps the `check-failure-triage:pr=` marker and the `- **Pull request:**` line, so when it is blocked and re-issued, the replacement gets "- Integration branch: `<example PR head ref>`". The replacement has no base marker and no ai:check-triage label, so it never reaches the `base` verdict in scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:343-347.
  WHY: The re-issued fix for a broken default branch is planned and implemented on an unrelated example PR's head branch, landing commits on someone else's PR branch. The file is outside the plan grant, so a follow-up issue may be needed.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:2596-2598,2299-2310 (with .github/workflows/plan.yml:1944-1956,1985-1988) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A base-keyed issue body has a `- **Base branch:**` line but no Target branch or Integration branch line, because the check at 2306 refuses routing coexistence. The resolver's `base` verdict (scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:482-486) prints nothing, so plan records `resolver_status=none`.
  WHY: With CHECK_TRIAGE_BRANCH_GUARD_ENABLED=true, plan.yml blocks every base-keyed issue (`outcome=blocked reason=no_target_branch_metadata`). This makes base-keyed triage incompatible with the branch guard. The limitation is documented at README.md:2019-2020 and changelog.d/9674-triage-base-keyed-fingerprint.md:17.
- README.md / changelog.d/9674-triage-base-keyed-fingerprint.md (behaviour driven by .github/workflows/plan.yml:1985 and scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:478-487) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The changelog says "What this means for operators: nothing to do". But consumers that run CHECK_TRIAGE_BRANCH_GUARD_ENABLED=true together with CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING_ENABLED=true now have every base-keyed issue blocked at plan; before, those issues were routed as `pr_head_routed`.
  WHY: For those consumers, a broken default branch is never auto-fixed until an operator edits the issue. The behaviour is documented, so this is a NIT, but the operator line is wrong.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Otherwise, file one issue for the base branch. Its body names the failing PR only as an example ("first seen on PR #N"), and its fix targets the base branch."
  expected_change_site: scripts/unblock_actions.py ci_owner_candidate / reissue branch (lines 253-271, 1120, 1132-1136), or scripts/unblock_judge.sh unblock_resolve_ci_owner (lines 1557-1656)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Only scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh learned the line-5 base marker, and no PR hunk touches scripts/unblock_actions.py or scripts/unblock_judge.sh (neither is in the plan grant's files_touched). ci_owner_candidate (scripts/unblock_actions.py:256) still resolves the example PR from the kept `pr=` marker. scripts/unblock_actions.py:1132-1136 then appends `- Integration branch: <example PR head ref>` without the base marker or the ai:check-triage label, so the `base` verdict in scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh (lines 339-347, 482-487) is never reached.
- requirement: "two different PRs failing the same check against a failing base → one issue total" (issue Tests section and Goal 1)
  expected_change_site: Post step in .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml (re-match before `gh issue create`), plus a concurrent-run test in tests/test_check_failure_triage_base_fingerprint.py
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: test_base_keyed_issue_from_another_pr_covers_this_pr only covers the case where the first issue is already in the listing. No code or test covers two overlapping runs, and the per-PR concurrency group does not serialize them.
- requirement: "If OPEN_TRIAGE already has an issue with that fingerprint: file nothing... and exit 0."
  expected_change_site: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh (post stage scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:2676-2682)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The dedup check reads a stale snapshot, so concurrent runs miss each other's issue and the implementation fails Goal 1 ("one breakage files one issue") under load.
- requirement: "Open-issue cap. New env var CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_MAX_OPEN_ISSUES ... default 5 ... When the count is at or above the cap, file nothing ... A supersede files a new issue and then closes the old one, so the open count doesn't grow." (linked issue Goal 3)
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml Post step (around lines 819-821), or a fresh `gh api` listing just before `gh issue create`
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The cap reads OPEN_TRIAGE once at scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1447 and counts it at scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1789. The post step at .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:819-821 creates the issue without listing or counting again, so concurrent runs can each pass the cap. The supersede exemption at scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1783 is undermined when a candidate is dropped by the base_triage_tracked early exit.
- requirement: "Its fix targets the base branch."
  expected_change_site: Generated issue branch metadata in scripts/check_failure_triage.sh, or the check-triage target-branch guard in .github/workflows/plan.yml
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The base-keyed issue body has no "Target branch:" or "Integration branch:" line, and the resolver produces no resolved branch status. With CHECK_TRIAGE_BRANCH_GUARD_ENABLED=true, plan.yml blocks `resolver_status=none`, and the PR documents this but gives base-keyed issues no path through the guard. Severity disagreement: google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite rated it BLOCKER, openai_gpt-6-luna MAJOR. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly judged this not a gap because the requirement is met with the guard off (the default) and the guard-on behaviour is documented.
- requirement: "When the base gate's conclusion is a completed non-success (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, …), use" the base-keyed fingerprint.
  expected_change_site: The base-conclusion case in scripts/check_failure_triage.sh and its tests
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1723-1742 base-keys only failure, timed_out, cancelled, startup_failure and action_required. tests/test_check_failure_triage_base_fingerprint.py:124-131 keeps neutral, skipped and stale on the per-PR fingerprint. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly judged this not a gap (a conservative reading; README.md:2003-2005 lists the exact set).
- requirement: "A base-keyed issue must still pass the post step's marker check (`<!-- check-failure-triage:fp=<fp> -->` on the first line, verified against `triage_metadata.json`)." (linked issue Constraints)
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml Post step (around lines 783-793)
  confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The post step regex-checks `triage_post_base_ref` (.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:788) but never compares it with the body's line-5 `<!-- check-failure-triage:base=<ref> -->`. scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:2299-2310 does not extract line 5 again either, so a forged triage_metadata.json could make the title and body disagree.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:1120 and 1132-1136 (owner from scripts/unblock_actions.py:253-271 ci_owner_candidate; scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1637-1643) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When a blocked base-keyed triage issue is re-issued, the replacement carries "- Integration branch: `<example PR head ref>`" and has no base marker and no ai:check-triage label, so it never reaches the `base` verdict in scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:343-347.
  WHY: The fix for a broken default branch lands on an unrelated PR's head branch. Suggested fix: ci_owner_candidate returns {"pr": None, "reason": "base_keyed"} when the line-5 base marker is present. The file is outside the plan grant, so a follow-up issue may be needed.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1471-1484 followed by 1729-1734 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When a stale ai:blocked per-PR issue qualifies for supersede and a base-keyed issue is already open, the run exits on base_triage_tracked without filing or closing anything.
  WHY: The stale issue stays open and counts toward the CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_MAX_OPEN_ISSUES cap (line 1789). Suggested fix: log `stale=${SUPERSEDE_OLD_ISSUE}`, or accept and document the behaviour.
- README.md / changelog.d/9674-triage-base-keyed-fingerprint.md (behaviour driven by .github/workflows/plan.yml:1985 and scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:478-487) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: With guard=true plus routing=true, base-keyed issues are now blocked at plan, where before they were routed as `pr_head_routed`.
  WHY: Those consumers never get the default branch auto-fixed, yet the changelog says "nothing to do".
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1447-1461, 1727-1735, 1789-1791; check_failure_triage.yml:234, 819-821 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The shared base-keyed fingerprint is matched and capped against a single stale snapshot, while the concurrency group isolates only one PR and check.
  WHY: Concurrent runs file duplicate issues and overshoot the cap, which breaks Goal 1 and "17 before, 1 now". Suggested fix: in the post step, when base_keyed_ref is set, list issues again and skip with `base_triage_tracked`.
- TASK_GAP Requirement: "Otherwise, file one issue for the base branch ... its fix targets
